title: Event-store migrations run through a release entry point, not mix
rationale: Local development and the integration tests both shell out to 'mix ecto.migrate', which hides this gap: the migration path works everywhere except the artifact that actually ships. Any future migration must be reachable from the release, not just from the mix project.

description: ForemanServer.Http.Endpoint hard-coded its Bandit bind address to {127,0,0,1} with no override, so a container's published port and a k8s Service could never reach the API. The failure mode is a silent TIMEOUT rather than an error, which reads like a cluster networking or Service-selector problem — the server logs look completely healthy and /api/v1/health answers fine from inside the container.
resolution: Added FOREMAN_SERVER_HTTP_BIND (ForemanServer.Http.Endpoint.bind_ip/0), which still DEFAULTS TO LOOPBACK and falls back to loopback on an unparseable value; the container image sets 0.0.0.0. The pre-existing validate_remote_access!/1 guard is what makes widening safe: binding beyond loopback without FOREMAN_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN raises at startup (verified exit 1 in the container, not just in tests). Keep that pairing — a wider default bind without the token guard would expose the orchestrator control plane unauthenticated.
